name: RAD-140

lead: RAD-140 (testolone, vosilasarm) is an oral selective androgen receptor modulator that lifters use for muscle and fat loss, with some hoping for less suppression than steroids.

It binds the androgen receptor with tissue selectivity. Rat and monkey studies showed muscle-stimulating effects with weaker effects on the prostate. It is under development by Ellipses Pharma for androgen receptor-positive breast cancer, and the only completed human trial was a small first-in-human study in postmenopausal women with breast cancer. No human data on its effect on lean body mass have been published.

paras: Sold online as a research chemical and taken orally during bulks or cuts, often over several weeks. Users judge it by strength and leanness changes.

Not approved for physique use and banned in sport. Case reports describe drug-induced liver injury, myocarditis and heart failure in non-medical users, and it suppresses natural hormones. Many products sold as a specific SARM contain none of it or unrelated substances.

angle.text: RAD-140 is a potent SARM used by lifters for more muscle and less fat, with some hoping for less suppression than steroids. It activates the androgen receptor in muscle. It has been studied in animals and is in development for breast cancer; human data on physique are lacking, and liver and hormone effects are reported.

lead: RAD-140, whose International Nonproprietary Name is vosilasarm and which is also sold under the names RAD140, Testolone and Testalone, is an orally taken, nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM). In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities it is used with the aim of adding lean muscle and a harder, leaner physique: more muscle on the frame changes shoulder, chest and arm proportions, and a lower body-fat percentage sharpens definition in the face and torso.[1][2] Those who use it generally combine it with resistance training and a calorie surplus or a cut, and often with other compounds.[2][3][4]

The molecule was designed by Radius Health in 2010 and described in a 2011 paper on its design, synthesis and preclinical characterisation.[1][5] It is now under development by Ellipses Pharma for androgen receptor-positive, estrogen receptor-negative, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, after earlier plans for sarcopenia, osteoporosis and cancer cachexia were dropped.[1] The only completed human trial is a first-in-human phase 1 dose-escalation study in 22 postmenopausal women with metastatic breast cancer, published in 2022.[6] No trial has measured its effect on muscle or fat in healthy people.[1]

RAD-140 is not approved for any medical use and is on the World Anti-Doping Agency's prohibited list.[1][7] It is sold online as a research chemical or supplement, and published case reports describe drug-induced liver injury, myocarditis and heart failure in people who used it for physique purposes.[8][9][10][11][12][13] Wikipedia notes that many products sold online as a specific SARM contain none of it or unrelated substances, and that social media has been important in spreading non-medical SARM use.[1]
infobox: About 45 to 60 hours[1]; 44.7 hours in the phase 1 trial[6]
Not approved for any medical use; prohibited by WADA[1][7]

paras: Vosilasarm is not approved for any medical use. Development for hormone-sensitive breast cancer is ongoing, and a phase 1/2 study proposal published in 2023 planned to recruit up to 128 patients.[1] Earlier development goals included age-related muscle loss (sarcopenia), osteoporosis and weight loss from cancer cachexia; the 2011 paper said cachexia studies were being prepared, but they were not completed or published.[1][5]

Wikipedia states that the compound is sold by black-market internet suppliers for physique and performance enhancement, often at doses that have not been evaluated in clinical trials, and that social media has played an important role in spreading non-medical SARM use.[1] The general appeal described by users is an oral, non-injected option marketed as muscle-selective, with posters framing it as a way to push past a lifting plateau or to add size during a bulk or retain muscle during a cut.[2][3]

On T Nation, posters mention it as a fat-loss or muscle option, as something a gym partner takes between cycles with MK-677, in connection with a competitive athlete's reported use, or during recovery attempts after a testosterone cycle.[14][15][16][17] Looksmax.org threads describe it alongside other SARMs, MK-677, dutasteride, isotretinoin, enclomiphene and testosterone, usually as one part of a larger stack.[2][3][4][18]

The first-in-human trial (NCT03088527) was a phase 1 study in postmenopausal women with ER-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer, started in October 2017 and completed in 2020.[19][19] It used a 3+3 dose-escalation design with a pharmacokinetic expansion cohort and enrolled 22 heavily pretreated women, 21 of them androgen receptor-positive, who took once-daily oral doses of 50, 100 or 150 mg; the maximum tolerated dose was 100 mg per day and the half-life was 44.7 hours.[6] Serum SHBG fell in all 18 evaluable patients and PSA rose in 16 of 20, which the authors used as markers that the drug engaged the androgen receptor.[6]

In that study the most common adverse events were raised AST (59.1 percent), raised ALT (45.5 percent), raised bilirubin (27.3 percent), vomiting, dehydration and decreased appetite and weight (27.3 percent each); grade 3 or 4 events occurred in 72.7 percent of patients, mainly liver enzyme rises and low phosphate.[6] One patient with an ESR1 mutation had a partial response, the 24-week clinical benefit rate was 18.2 percent and median progression-free survival was 2.3 months; the authors concluded the safety profile was acceptable with preliminary evidence of target engagement and antitumor activity.[6]

No clinical trial has tested RAD-140 for muscle building or appearance in healthy people. The doses discussed in non-medical use differ from the cancer trial regimens and their effects are unknown.[1] A human study of micro-dosed RAD140 has been published for doping-control purposes, focusing on how the body metabolises and eliminates it rather than on body composition.[20]

Preclinical work includes the 2011 characterisation in rats and monkeys, a 2017 Clinical Cancer Research study in which oral RAD140 activated the androgen receptor in breast cancer cells but not prostate cancer cells and slowed growth of patient-derived androgen- and estrogen-receptor-positive xenografts, and a cell-based and in silico study comparing RAD-140 with two other SARMs.[5][21][22] A 2023 study found that 10 weeks of RAD140 in female mice negatively affected skeletal muscle adaptation, frailty status and mortality risk.[23] In cynomolgus monkeys, vosilasarm cut testosterone by about half and altered lipids.[1] A 2025 Physiological Reports paper assessed RAD140 for muscle mass and bone mineral density in a preclinical setting.[20]

Liver injury is the most documented harm from non-medical use. Case reports include a 24-year-old man with cholestatic liver injury confirmed on biopsy after five weeks of use, a 29-year-old with jaundice after about three months, and a 52-year-old man who used two supplements containing RAD-140 or RAD-140 with LGD-4033, with liver enzymes returning to normal about three months after stopping.[8][12][13] A further report and literature review covers SARM-induced liver injury more broadly.[24]

Cardiac cases have also been reported: a 16-year-old boy with myopericarditis after a first dose, a young man with acute myocarditis, and a case described as heart failure from SARM abuse.[9][10][11] The authors of the myopericarditis report note that the drugs' side effects, which can be life-threatening, are not well characterized.[9]

Hormonal effects are documented in both the cancer trial (lower SHBG, higher PSA) and monkeys (testosterone roughly halved).[1][6] A forum poster described suppressed testosterone and cholesterol after a cycle of two SARMs at doses lower than lifters recommended, and others report erectile and libido problems after use.[25][17] Wikipedia says masculinisation and long-term effects are unknown.[1] Looksmax.org users who report positive experiences often describe taking additional drugs to manage side effects, which is itself a sign of the multi-compound practice in these communities.[2]

RAD-140 is a tissue-selective agonist or partial agonist of the androgen receptor. It binds with a Ki of about 7 nM (versus 10 nM for DHT) and good selectivity over other steroid receptors.[1] In castrated rats it stimulated levator ani muscle at a dose far below that needed to affect prostate weight, a roughly 33-fold difference, and in young monkeys it dose-dependently increased body weight and numerically increased lean mass.[1] Combined with testosterone it partly antagonised prostate and seminal vesicle weight gain while adding to muscle weight in rats.[1] Agonist effects in androgen receptor-expressing breast cancer cell lines underlie its investigation in breast cancer.[1][21]

Oral bioavailability was 27 to 63 percent in rats and 65 to 75 percent in monkeys; the human elimination half-life is reported as 45 to 60 hours, and the phase 1 trial measured 44.7 hours.[1][6] Metabolism has been studied in horses, in vitro systems and humans largely to build doping-control tests.[26][20]

Vosilasarm is an oxadiazole aniline derivative; other aniline SARMs include AC-262536 and ACP-105.[1] The SARM class began with nonsteroidal compounds made in 1998 independently by a University of Tennessee group and by Ligand Pharmaceuticals, and the term selective androgen receptor modulator was introduced in 1999 by Negro-Vilar, by analogy with SERMs.[27]

Radius Health developed RAD140 in 2010, and the 2011 ACS Medicinal Chemistry Letters paper on its design, synthesis and preclinical characterisation presented it as a potent, orally active nonsteroidal SARM in preclinical models of anabolic and androgenic activity.[1][5] Phase 1 studies for cancer cachexia were said to be in preparation but were not completed or published, and the compound was repurposed for breast cancer.[1] A 2017 Clinical Cancer Research paper described its activity in AR- and ER-positive breast cancer models, the first-in-human study began in October 2017 and finished in 2020, and results were published from 2019 to 2022; a phase 1/2 study proposal followed in 2023.[1][19][21][6]

Meanwhile RAD-140 became one of a small group of SARMs, with enobosarm (ostarine), LGD-4033 (ligandrol) and andarine, that are most commonly sold online and discussed by lifters.[1] Anti-doping bodies recorded their first adverse analytical finding for a SARM in 2010, and the number of positive tests has risen since.[27] Analytical papers list ligandrol, ostarine, RAD-140 and andarine as the most popular agents of the class.[28]

As of 2023 neither the US FDA nor the European Medicines Agency had approved any SARM for therapeutic use.[27] Wikipedia's SARM article says marketing SARMs for human consumption has led to criminal convictions in the United States and that Australia lists enobosarm as a prescription-only Schedule 4 substance.[27] Vosilasarm itself remains an investigational drug.[1]

SARMs were added to the WADA Prohibited List in 2008, are prohibited in and out of competition, and athletes in the NFL, NBA, UFC, NCAA and the Olympics have tested positive for SARMs according to Wikipedia.[7][28][27] Analytical papers describe detection methods, including equine metabolite studies, forensic follow-up of adverse findings and a nanoparticle sensor for RAD-140 and other SARMs in serum.[7][28][26][29]

subs.h: Product content and the grey market
paras: SARMs are sold on grey markets as research chemicals and promoted through online guides and social media.[27] Wikipedia reports that many products sold as a specific SARM contain none of it or something unrelated, and one case report involved branded supplements that combined RAD-140 with LGD-4033.[1][13][27]

subs.h: Use in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities
paras: On T Nation, posters ask whether others have tried RAD-140, mention using it with MK-677 between cycles, report one RAD-140 cycle in a year of SARM cycling, or ask about sourcing it; one poster said an article about a competitor's use made him want to take it.[14][15][16][30]

On looksmax.org, threads include a post-cycle results write-up in which the poster reports adding roughly 8 to 10 lb of muscle over eight weeks while training and taking other drugs and says side effects were minimal, requests for advice on pairing it with MK-677, discussion of transitioning between SARMs, and a post from a minor asking whether to take it.[2][3][4][18][31] Replies in these threads often argue about which SARM is better for bulking or why testosterone would not be preferred, showing that it is treated as one option among several.[3][4] Wikipedia's SARM article says that in a study of users more than 90 percent were satisfied and 64 percent would use SARMs again even though most reported adverse effects.[27]

Current work focuses on androgen receptor-positive breast cancer, where Ellipses Pharma is developing vosilasarm as EP0062.[1] Laboratory and analytical work continues on metabolism, biomarkers and detection for sport.[26][29][20] A published search of the literature on RAD140 shows case reports and doping-control studies growing alongside the cancer research.[20]

lore.intro: RAD-140 is discussed on forums as a potent oral SARM, often described alongside other compounds in bulking, recovery and cycling contexts, with results threads and requests for stacking advice.[15][16][25][2][3]
